Detailed Technical Scope

Section 1: Distributed training across thousands of GPUs using DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM, and PyTorch FSDP. The researcher will investigate architectural novelties in transformer blocks, attention routing, state space models, and mixture-of-experts routing layers. Analysis includes KV-cache compression, speculative decoding, and quantization-aware training at 4-bit and 8-bit precision.

Section 2: High throughput data pipelines and curation engines. Managing petabyte-scale token datasets, deduplication heuristics using MinHash and LSH, synthetic data generation pipelines, quality filtering with classifier ensembles, and tokenization benchmarking.

Section 3: Mathematical modeling of scaling laws, loss landscapes, and optimization dynamics. Evaluating learning rate schedulers, weight decay formulations, adaptive optimizers, and gradient clipping thresholds in multi-node clusters with tens of thousands of compute devices.

Requirements

  • PhD or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or related field.
  • Deep understanding of foundational transformer architectures and optimization theory.
  • Extensive track record of publication in top-tier machine learning venues (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).
  • Fluency in Python, CUDA, Triton, and high-performance distributed networking (NCCL, InfiniBand).

Responsibilities

  • Lead breakthrough research initiatives in foundation models.
  • Publish open source weights, code, and technical reports for the worldwide community.
  • Mentor junior researchers and collaborate with external academic labs.

Conclusion: We believe in open science and reproducible AI research. Join us in shaping the open future of artificial intelligence for all humanity. Continuous learning and competitive compensation packages are provided.
